h1: Thepnakorn Hotel Buriram — a veteran hotel in the city centre that's budget-friendly with lovely staff
intro: If you're in Buriram on a budget and want a big room, a pool to jump into, a generous breakfast and a central base — Thepnakorn Hotel is a veteran that's been part of the city since 1994. A 3-star, 175-room hotel on Jira Road, rooms start from approx. THB 700/night. The plus points are friendly staff and value for money, but be clear going in: the building is old and room condition is inconsistent — real reviews both praise and criticise it plainly.

body.html: Thepnakorn Hotel has been open since 1994 and was once one of Buriram's main hotels in its day, with its last major refurbishment around 2012. Its enduring strength is its central location on Jira Road, an easy hop to the market, restaurants and the government district. It's a large property of 175 rooms with facilities that are full for the price bracket — a pool, sauna, gym and massage rooms, which you rarely find in hotels this cheap.

Rooms come as Standard, Superior and Luxury/VIP. What guests agree on is that the rooms are spacious and high-ceilinged, with more floor space than newer hotels at the same price. Beds are comfortable, and there's a fridge, minibar and air conditioning throughout. But the design and furnishings are old-school, and some rooms still have the original carpet and wallpaper. Anyone expecting a sleek, modern room may find it dated, while those after a big room for little money usually call it good value.
"Lovely clean hotel, a good upgrade from a motel. The staff are friendly and helpful, and the breakfast is varied and tasty."

What draws the most praise is the friendly, helpful staff and the generous buffet breakfast that's better than the price suggests, with both Thai dishes and sweets. The large outdoor pool has a separate children's pool, making it good for families, and there's a sauna and massage rooms to relax in. Parking is spacious and free, and Wi-Fi is free in all rooms. For travellers who prioritise value and aren't fussed about newness, all of this together is a lot for the money.

To be clear about the downsides: plenty of reviews criticise the dated building and inconsistent cleanliness. Some guests report unclean bathrooms, a musty smell, grime in corners, weak air conditioning and low water pressure in certain rooms. Scores across platforms are accordingly scattered — around 7.2 on Booking, 5.9 on Trip.com and 2.7 out of 5 on TripAdvisor. This is a hotel where the experience depends a good deal on the room you get and the expectations you bring.

On location: it's genuinely central, but around 6 km from Chang Arena and Chang International Circuit. If you're here mainly for the football or racing, a hotel near the stadium is more convenient on event days. But if you're exploring the town, eating at the market, or using Buriram as a base for Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam, a central spot like this is easier to get around from. It's a short drive to the King Rama I Monument and Khao Kradong Forest Park.

The honest verdict: Thepnakorn Hotel suits budget travellers who value price, a big room and a central location over newness. If you can accept a veteran hotel and pick a renovated room, you'll get a good-value stay with lovely staff and a strong breakfast. But if you're sensitive about cleanliness or want a crisp, modern room, a newer city boutique like The Crystal or The Sita Princess may sit easier with you.

A tip from reading the reviews: ask for a renovated Superior or Luxury room, and view the room before checking in if you can — condition varies noticeably here. Check the air conditioning is cold and the bathroom is clean before you take it; if it isn't, ask to switch. The staff here are usually happy to help.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Thepnakorn Hotel Buriram

faq.q: Where is Thepnakorn Hotel and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 139 Jira Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Buriram, in the city centre. The King Rama I Monument and Sao Kraw Market are about 2 km away; Buriram Train Station is around 3 km, Chang Arena about 6 km, and Khao Kradong Forest Park about 7 km.

faq.q: What are the starting prices and room types?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 700/night for a Standard room. There are Standard, Superior, Luxury and VIP rooms (around THB 1,500). Prices depend on dates and Chang Arena event days, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is Thepnakorn Hotel old? What's the room condition like?
faq.a: The hotel has been open since 1994 and was last refurbished around 2012. Rooms are spacious and high-ceilinged, but the design and furnishings are dated and cleanliness is inconsistent. Ask for a renovated room and view it first — staff are happy to switch you if it isn't right.

faq.q: Is it a good base for events at Chang Arena?
faq.a: It's central, around 6 km from Chang Arena and the racing circuit. If you're here mainly for the football or racing, a hotel near the stadium is more convenient on event days. But for exploring the town, the market, or using Buriram as a base for Phanom Rung, this central spot is easier to get around from.

faq.q: Is there a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes — a large outdoor pool with a children's pool, an indoor pool, a sauna, gym and massage rooms. The varied buffet breakfast is a point reviews agree on, with Thai dishes and sweets. Check at booking whether your package includes breakfast.

faq.q: Who is Thepnakorn Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits budget travellers who value price, a big room and a central location over newness. You get lovely staff and a good breakfast. If you want a crisp, modern room, a newer city boutique like The Crystal or The Sita Princess may suit you better.
